text: RENTAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEM — RAG KNOWLEDGE BASE 1. System Overview The Rental Management System is a digital platform designed to manage rental products, customers, reservations, rental periods, returns, payments, penalties, notifications, and administrative operations. The system allows customers to register accounts, securely log in, manage their profiles, maintain residential and billing addresses, browse rental items, create rental requests, manage active rentals, return rented items, and receive notifications. Administrators can manage customers, rental items, rental requests, bookings, rental transactions, returns, penalties, deposits, payments, notifications, and audit records. The system separates authentication data, customer profile data, rental data, payment data, and audit data.

The system must not store unnecessary sensitive information. 2. Customer Registration A customer must create an account before using rental services that require authentication. The registration process may require: First name Last name Email address Mobile number Password Password confirmation The email address should be unique. Customers must provide accurate information during registration. The system may require email verification before activating the account. If an email address is already registered, the system should prevent duplicate registration. The system should not expose existing account information to unauthorized users. • • • • • • 1 3. Email Verification Email verification confirms that the customer controls the email address provided during registration.

The system may send a verification code or verification link to the registered email address. Verification codes must have an expiration period. An expired verification code must not be accepted. Customers may request a new verification code when the previous code expires. The system should limit repeated verification requests to prevent abuse. 4. Login Users can log into the Rental Management System using their registered email address and password. The login process should verify: Email address Password Account status Account lock status Authentication requirements If the credentials are valid, the system creates an authenticated session. The system may issue an access token and refresh token. If authentication fails, the system should return a generic message.

Example: Invalid email or password. The system should not reveal whether a particular email address exists. 5. Login Security The Rental Management System should protect customer accounts against unauthorized access. Security mechanisms may include: Password hashing • • • • • • 2 Access tokens Refresh tokens Token expiration Failed login tracking Temporary account locking Device identification IP address tracking User-agent tracking Suspicious login detection Audit logging Passwords must never be stored as plain text. Authentication credentials must not be exposed in normal API responses. 6. Failed Login Attempts The system may track failed login attempts. Repeated failed login attempts may indicate an attempted unauthorized login.

The system may temporarily lock an account after a configured number of failed login attempts. The lock duration should be configurable. A successful login may reset the failed login counter. Example security message: Too many unsuccessful login attempts. Please try again later. 7. Account Locking A locked account cannot perform normal authentication until the lock period expires or an authorized administrator unlocks the account. Account locking helps protect accounts from brute-force attacks. The system may store: Failed login count Lock status Lock expiration time Last failed login time Administrators may investigate suspicious account activity through audit logs. • • • • • • • • • • • • • • 3 8. Access Token An access token is used to authenticate requests to protected API endpoints.

Protected API requests may contain: Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN Access tokens should have a limited lifetime. The backend must verify the access token before processing protected operations. Expired or invalid access tokens must be rejected. 9. Refresh Token A refresh token may be used to obtain a new access token after the access token expires. Refresh tokens normally have a longer lifetime than access tokens. Refresh tokens should be securely managed. The system should preferably store a secure hash of refresh tokens rather than storing raw refresh tokens. Expired, revoked, or invalid refresh tokens must not be accepted. 10. Logout Users should be able to log out of the Rental Management System.

During logout, the current authentication session or refresh token should be invalidated when applicable. The client should remove locally stored authentication credentials after logout. After logout, protected API requests should require authentication again. 11. Forgot Password Users who forget their password may request a password reset. The system may send a password-reset link or verification code to the registered email address. Password-reset tokens must have an expiration period. 4 Expired password-reset tokens must not be accepted. A password-reset token should only be usable according to the configured reset policy. After successfully changing the password, previously active authentication sessions may be revoked for security. 12.

Password Change Authenticated users may change their password from their account settings. The user should normally provide: Current password New password New password confirmation The new password must satisfy the system's password requirements. The system must never store the password in plain text. 13. User Profile A customer profile may contain: First name Last name Mobile number Date of birth Profile image Biography Residential address Billing address Customers should keep their profile information accurate. Profile information should only be accessible according to the user's permissions. 14. Residential Address The residential address represents the customer's current living address.

The address may contain: Address line 1 Address line 2 • • • • • • • • • • • • • 5 City Province or State Postal code Country The residential address may be used for customer identification, delivery, communication, or rental-related services. Example: Address Line 1: No. 25, Peradeniya Road Address Line 2: Near Kandy City Centre City: Kandy Province: Central Province Postal Code: 20000 Country: Sri Lanka 15. Billing Address The billing address represents the address associated with billing and invoices. The billing address can be different from the residential address. For example, a customer may live in Kandy while using a billing address in Colombo. Residential and billing addresses must be maintained independently.

Changing the residential address must not automatically change the billing address. Changing the billing address must not automatically change the residential address. Example: Billing Address Line 1: No. 142, Galle Road Billing Address Line 2: Colombo 03 City: Colombo Province: Western Province Postal Code: 00300 Country: Sri Lanka 16. Payment Security The Rental Management System should not store raw credit-card or debit-card information. • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • 6 The system must not store: Full card numbers CVV numbers Card PINs Card passwords Payment authentication secrets Payment processing should be handled by an appropriate external payment provider.

The rental application may store safe payment references such as: Payment provider Transaction reference Payment status Amount Currency Payment timestamp Payment information should remain separate from the customer profile. 17. Rental Item A rental item is a product, vehicle, property, equipment item, tool, or other asset that can be rented. A rental item may contain: Item name Description Category Rental price Pricing period Availability status Condition Images Location Owner Security deposit Rental rules Each rental item should have a unique identifier. 18. Rental Item Availability An item is available when it can be rented during the requested period. The system must check availability before confirming a rental.

• • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • 7 A physical item should not normally be assigned to multiple customers during overlapping rental periods. Possible statuses include: Available Reserved Rented Maintenance Unavailable Retired Items marked as maintenance should normally not be available for new rentals. 19. Rental Booking A customer creates a rental booking when they request to rent an item. A booking may contain: Customer Rental item Start date End date Rental duration Rental price Deposit Booking status Additional notes The system should validate the requested rental period. The system should verify item availability before confirming the booking. 20. Rental Status A rental can have different statuses during its lifecycle.

Pending The customer has submitted a rental request, but it has not yet been confirmed. Confirmed The rental has been approved and reserved for the customer. • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • 8 Active The customer has received the rental item and the rental period has started. Completed The customer has returned the item and the rental process has been completed. Cancelled The rental was cancelled before completion. Overdue The agreed return date has passed and the item has not been returned. 21. Rental Pickup Before handing over an item, staff should verify the rental information.

The system may record: Customer information Rental information Pickup date Pickup time Item condition Included accessories Photos Staff member responsible for handover The customer should be informed about important rental rules before receiving the item. 22. Rental Return Customers must return rented items on or before the agreed rental end date and time. The returned item should be inspected. The system may record: Return date Return time Item condition Damage Missing accessories • • • • • • • • • • • • • 9 Late-return information Additional charges The rental should be marked as completed only after the return process has been properly recorded. 23. Late Return A rental becomes overdue when the customer does not return the item within the agreed rental period.

A late return may result in additional charges or penalties. The system should record: Expected return date Expected return time Actual return date Actual return time Overdue duration Applicable penalty Customers should be notified when a rental becomes overdue. 24. Important Return Notice Customers must return rental items before or at the agreed rental end date and time. Failure to return an item on time may result in additional charges or penalties. Customers who require additional rental time should request an extension before the rental period expires. 25. Rental Extension A customer may request an extension when they need to keep an item longer than the original rental period. An extension request should preferably be submitted before the original rental period expires.

An extension depends on item availability. If another customer has reserved the item, the extension may be rejected. Approved extensions may generate additional rental charges. • • • • • • • • 10 26. Rental Cancellation A customer may cancel a rental according to the configured cancellation policy. Cancellation rules may depend on how much time remains before the rental start date. Possible cancellation statuses include: Cancellation requested Cancellation approved Cancellation rejected Cancelled Any applicable cancellation charge or refund must follow the configured rental policy. 27. Security Deposit Some rental items may require a security deposit.

A security deposit is intended to protect the rental provider against risks such as: Damage Loss Missing accessories Failure to return the item The deposit amount may vary depending on the rental item. The security deposit should be treated separately from the normal rental price. After the item is returned and inspected, the deposit may be released according to the rental agreement. 28. Damaged Rental Item If a rental item is returned damaged, the damage should be recorded. A damage record may include: Rental ID Item ID Damage description Damage severity Photos Inspection date Estimated repair cost Customer notification • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • 11 Resolution status Applicable charges should follow the rental agreement. 29.

Missing Rental Item If a customer does not return a rental item, the rental may be marked as overdue or missing. The customer should be contacted. The system should record communication and actions taken. If the item cannot be recovered, the case may be escalated according to the rental provider's policies. 30. Rental Pricing Rental pricing may be calculated using: Hourly rates Daily rates Weekly rates Monthly rates Seasonal rates Promotional rates Customer-specific pricing The applicable rental price should be displayed before the customer confirms the rental. Additional charges should be clearly identified. 31. Rental Price Example An item has a daily rental price of LKR 2,000. The customer rents the item for three days.

Base rental amount: 3 × LKR 2,000 = LKR 6,000 If a late-return penalty of LKR 1,000 is applicable: Additional penalty: LKR 1,000 Total applicable amount: LKR 7,000 • • • • • • • • 12 Actual charges must always follow the configured rental policy. 32. Customer Responsibilities Customers are responsible for: Providing accurate account information Maintaining accurate billing information Using rental items correctly Following rental instructions Returning items on time Returning all included accessories Reporting damage Reporting problems Protecting rental items Following the rental agreement Customers must not intentionally misuse rental items. 33.

Rental Provider Responsibilities Rental providers are responsible for: Providing accurate rental-item information Maintaining availability information Providing items in the agreed condition Recording item condition Managing rental requests Managing returns Handling customer support Maintaining rental records Applying rental policies consistently 34. Notifications The system may send notifications for: Registration Email verification Successful login Password changes Rental request creation Rental approval Rental rejection Rental starting soon Rental ending soon • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • 13 Rental overdue Rental return Payment status Cancellation Account status changes Notifications should clearly explain the event and any required customer action. 35.

Rental Reminder Example notification: Rental Return Reminder Your rental is scheduled to end soon. Please return the rented item before the agreed return date and time to avoid additional charges or late-return penalties. 36. Overdue Notification Example notification: Rental Overdue Your rental return deadline has passed. Please return the rented item as soon as possible. Additional charges may apply according to the rental agreement. 37. Account Status A customer account may be active or disabled. An active account can use the system according to its permissions. A disabled account should not be allowed to perform operations requiring an active account. Administrators may disable an account when required. Account status changes should be recorded in the audit log. 38.

Roles The system may contain different roles. • • • • • 14 Customer Customers can manage their own profile, browse rental items, create bookings, manage rentals, and view their own rental information. Administrator Administrators can manage users, rental items, bookings, returns, penalties, and system operations. Staff Staff members may handle item pickup, item return, inspection, and rental operations. Manager Managers may have higher-level operational permissions such as monitoring rentals, managing staff, and reviewing reports. Permissions should be controlled using role-based access control. 39. Audit Logs An audit log records important actions performed in the system.

Examples include: Login Logout Failed login Profile update Password change Account status change Rental creation Rental approval Rental cancellation Rental extension Rental return Penalty creation Administrative changes An audit log may contain: User Action Description IP address User agent • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • 15 Timestamp Additional metadata Audit logs help administrators investigate security incidents and system activity. 40. Customer Privacy Customers should only be able to access their own private information unless they have appropriate administrative permissions.

A customer must not be allowed to access another customer's: Password Authentication tokens Billing information Rental history Personal address Private profile information Payment details Administrators should only access private information when required for legitimate system operations. 41. Data Separation The system should separate different types of information. Customer profile data should contain customer information. Rental data should contain rental information. Payment data should contain payment-related information. Authentication data should contain authentication information. Audit data should contain system activity. Raw payment-card information should not be stored in the customer profile. 42.

Customer Support Customers may contact support regarding: Account problems Login problems Rental availability Booking problems • • • • • • • • • • • • • 16 Rental extensions Returns Late returns Damage Billing Payment status Cancellation Refund status The chatbot should provide general information using the knowledge base. Customer-specific information should be retrieved from authorized application services. 43. Frequently Asked Questions Q: Can my billing address be different from my residential address? A: Yes. The billing address and residential address are separate and can contain different information. Q: Can I change my billing address? A: Yes. Customers can update their billing address when profile updates are permitted.

Q: Can I extend my rental? A: A rental extension may be requested before the rental period expires. Approval depends on item availability and the rental policy. Q: What happens if I return an item late? A: The rental may become overdue and additional charges or penalties may apply. Q: What happens if I damage a rental item? A: The damage may be recorded during the return inspection and applicable charges may be applied according to the rental agreement. Q: Can I cancel my rental? A: Rental cancellation is subject to the configured cancellation policy. Q: Does the system store my card number? A: The rental system should not store raw card numbers or CVV information. Payment processing should be handled securely by an appropriate payment provider.

• • • • • • • • 17 Q: What happens after I return an item? A: The item is inspected, the return is recorded, applicable charges are calculated, and the rental can be marked as completed. Q: Why can't I log in? A: Check that your email and password are correct. If the account is locked, disabled, or requires verification, follow the appropriate account-recovery or verification process. Q: What should I do if I forget my password? A: Use the password-reset process to request a password reset through the registered email address. 44. Example Customer Scenario Customer: Kasun Perera Residential Address: Kandy, Sri Lanka Billing Address: Colombo, Sri Lanka Kasun wants to rent a professional camera for three days. The customer logs into the Rental Management System.

The customer searches for available cameras. The customer selects an available camera. The customer requests a rental from August 20 to August 23. The system checks availability. The rental is approved. The camera is handed over to the customer on August 20. The customer uses the camera during the agreed rental period. The customer returns the camera on August 23. Staff inspect the camera. No damage is identified. 18 The rental is marked as completed. 45. Example Overdue Scenario Customer: Nadeesha Fernando Rental Item: Professional Camera Rental Start: August 20 at 10:00 AM Expected Return: August 22 at 6:00 PM Actual Return: August 24 at 10:00 AM The rental is overdue because the customer did not return the camera before the agreed return time. The system records the overdue period.

The applicable late-return charge is calculated according to the rental policy. The customer receives an overdue notification. 46. Example Address Scenario A customer has the following residential address: No. 25, Peradeniya Road Kandy Central Province 20000 Sri Lanka The customer's billing address is: No. 142, Galle Road Colombo 03 Western Province 00300 Sri Lanka The system stores these addresses independently. Updating the residential address does not automatically update the billing address. Updating the billing address does not automatically update the residential address. 19 47. Chatbot Knowledge Rules The rental chatbot should answer general rental questions using information retrieved from the RAG knowledge base.

The chatbot should provide accurate answers based on retrieved documents. The chatbot must not invent: Rental prices Penalties Availability Booking status Payment status Refund amounts Customer information Rental policies If the knowledge base does not contain enough information, the chatbot should clearly state that the required information is unavailable. The chatbot should not pretend to know information that is not available. 48. RAG and Live Database Data The RAG vector database should primarily contain general and relatively stable knowledge.

Examples include: Rental policies Return policies Cancellation policies Account policies Security policies Payment rules Frequently asked questions User guides System instructions Rental procedures MongoDB or another operational database should remain the source of truth for live information. Examples of live information include: Current user account Current rental Current booking • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • 20 Current item availability Current rental price Current payment status Current penalty Current return status The chatbot should combine RAG knowledge with authorized application APIs when answering customer- specific questions. 49.

Customer-Specific Questions Questions such as: "What is my current rental?" "Where is my booking?" "When do I need to return my rental?" "How much do I currently owe?" "Is my rental overdue?" "What is the status of my payment?" "What items have I rented?" should not be answered only using the vector database. The chatbot should retrieve the customer's authenticated information from the application backend. The chatbot must verify the customer's identity and permissions before returning private information. 50.

RAG Document Categories Recommended knowledge categories include: Authentication Registration Login Security Password Account Profile Address Billing Rental Booking Availability Pricing Pickup Return Late Return • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • 21 Extension Cancellation Deposit Damage Payment Notification Support Administration Audit Privacy FAQ Each document or chunk should contain useful metadata. Example metadata: Document Type: rental_policy Category: return Title: Late Return Policy Version: 1.0 Source: Rental Management System Knowledge Base 51. Chatbot Security The chatbot must not expose confidential system information.

The chatbot must not reveal: Database credentials API secrets JWT secrets Password hashes Authentication tokens Internal security keys Private customer data Other customers' information Payment-card information The chatbot should follow the permissions of the authenticated user. A customer should only receive information that the customer is authorized to access. 52. Unknown Questions If a user asks a question that is not covered by the knowledge base, the chatbot should not invent an answer. • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • 22 Example response: "I don't have enough information in the available rental-system knowledge base to answer that accurately." The chatbot may recommend contacting rental support when appropriate. 53.

RAG Response Principle The chatbot should retrieve the most relevant knowledge chunks before generating an answer. The retrieved information should be used as the primary source for general rental-policy questions. The chatbot should avoid irrelevant information. The chatbot should provide concise answers unless the customer requests additional details. For policy questions, the chatbot should explain the applicable rule clearly. For customer-specific questions, the chatbot should use authorized live application data. 54. General Rental Policy Customers must follow the rental agreement associated with each rental. Rental periods, prices, deposits, penalties, cancellation conditions, and return requirements may differ between rental items.

The specific rental agreement should take priority over general assumptions. Customers should review the rental conditions before confirming a rental. 55. Final System Principle The Rental Management System should provide a secure, reliable, and transparent rental experience. Customer information must be protected. Authentication information must be secured. Residential and billing addresses must remain separate. Payment-card information must not be stored in the customer profile. Rental information must be accurately maintained. 23 Returns and overdue rentals must be properly tracked. Penalties must follow configured rental policies. The AI chatbot must use RAG knowledge for general system information and authorized backend services for live customer-specific information. 24
